title: This Giant Bullseye Is So Big, Astronauts Use It As A Landmark
description:

scenes.text: There's a giant bullseye in the middle of the Sahara Desert, so large that astronauts have used it as a landmark from orbit. For decades, nobody could agree on what it actually was.
It's called the Richat Structure, and it's roughly forty kilometers across -- about twenty five miles wide, so large you can't actually tell what it is from ground level.
The first guess was an impact crater, since meteor strikes usually leave behind exactly this kind of circular shape.
But detailed studies never found any of the evidence a real impact actually leaves behind -- no shock-altered rock, no melted impact debris. It's not a crater at all.

The leading explanation now is that it's a dome of rock that got pushed up from below, then slowly eroded -- different rock layers wearing away at different rates is what carved out those perfect rings.
It's also become a magnet for a much wilder theory -- that it's the lost city of Atlantis, because its rings vaguely match Plato's original description. There's no real evidence for that either.
Would you have guessed this was natural, not something built?
